newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes says some weak markets persist.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes says some weak markets persist.

text.p: Great Lakes Chemical Corp said weak market conditions in certain sectors continue and may make 1997 as challenging as 1996.

In a statement, chief executive Robert McDonald said, "The year ahead could pose no less of a challenge considering that the weak market conditions in certain parts of our business have persisted into 1997."

He said initiatives to enhance profitability are underway, including cost reduction and assessment of the company's business portfolio. "Clearly, we are not satisfied with the status quo," McDonald said.
Great Lakes on Wednesday reported 1996 profits of $250 million on sales of $2.2 billion, compared with 1995 profits of $296 million on sales of $2.4 billion.
Fourth-quarter profits were $38 million on sales of $515 million, versus year-ago profits of $75 million on sales of $565 million, the specialty chemicals manufacturer said.

"The company's performance in the fourth quarter did not meet our expectations and fell short of the standards our shareholders expect from Great Lakes," McDonald said. "Lower earnings from our Octel Associates' tetraethyl lead business contributed to the disappointingly weak results."

In addition, the company said it took about $28 million in writeoffs, adjustments to reserves and other non-recurring expenses that more than offset a one-time gain on the year of $13 million from the sale of its E/M subsidiary.
"For the first time in 10 years of growth, Great Lakes sales and earnings did not exceed the prior year," he said.
The company said fourth-quarter tetraethyl lead sales increased from the third quarter, but "virtually all of the gain originated in low-margin wholesale markets."
"In the retail markets, order and shipping patterns combined to create a mix effect that resulted in lower earnings for the quarter," McDonald said.

Sales of flame retardants in the fourth quarter rose slightly from the third quarter. For the year, sales roughly equalled the 1995 level, the company said. "We have successfully defended market share during one of the most competitive periods in recent memory, but in doing so, diminished short-term profitability," McDonald said.
He added that weaker demand and pricing pressure in the furfural business continued in the fourth quarter, while currency fluctuations also "reduced profitability across all our business units."
Sales in the polymer stabilizers business rose on the year and the fourth quarter, he said.
